# Purpose of the document 

The purpose of this document is to create the different WEA scenarios, gather the projection data frame for the West Coast Groundfish Bottom Trawl Survey, and the coastline information.

WEAs will include 3 different scenarios. The first scenario includes the two leased WEAs in California (Morro Bay and Brookings) as well as the two Oregon call areas that were originally going up for auction in October of 2024 (Brooking and Coos Bay). While these two Oregon areas did not actually go to lease, this spatial scenario was considered the smallest and realistic. The second scenario includes these original 4 as well as five other considered areas identified in California (Del Norte, Humboldt 2, Humboldt 3, Mendocino 2, and Monterey - Mendocino 1 was not included because it does not overlap with the survey). The last scenario is the most extreme, but also based in reality. This includes the two large Oregon areas that were sized down to the original potential lease areas (large Coos Bay and large Brookings) and the large areas in California that were the based on the areas of interest in scenario 2 (Del Norte Oval, Humboldt Oval, Morro Bay oval).


### Projection data frame

The projection area considered was largely left alone with the exception of removing a few grid cells that are offshore in the southern district. These areas were not sampled in the 2003-2023 time period, and also have a major impact on previous analyses. For these reasons I removed these 7 grid cells from the projection. 

One important variable to include in both the projection dataset and the OSW shapefile is "group". This is the separating variable within the sdmTMB function written, so be sure to label the projection dataset "group" the "Entire region" and each individual OSW shapefile polygons as individual groups.

```{r Projection_dataset, message=FALSE, fig.height=3, fig.width=5, fig.cap= "\\label{fig::R} Spatial extent of the Projection data frame including A) the removed areas - red - and B) the spatial extent with the area removed."}
#### Coast outline - for plotting 
coast_outline <- ne_states(country = 'United States of America', returnclass = 'sf') %>%
  filter(gn_name %in% c('California','Oregon','Washington','Nevada','Idaho', "Montana")) %>%
  st_transform(crs = "+proj=utm +zone=10 +datum=WGS84 +units=km")#make sure to convernt to UTM 

####Projection shapefile and dataframe - for predictions and plotting. HM: edited file path to match repo folders
Projection_extent = read_sf(paste0(WD.1,"/Data_shapefiles/WCGBTS_Grid_v2008_GCSWGS84.shp")) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude")) %>%
  st_transform(crs = st_crs("+proj=utm +zone=10 +datum=WGS84 +units=km"))
Projection_extent$Area_km2 = Projection_extent$Area_sqm*0.000001 #grab the area for each cell - change from m^2 to km^2
saveRDS(Projection_extent, paste0(WD.1, "/Data_shapefiles/Projection_shapefile_WCGBTWS.rds"))


Proj_df = as.data.frame(Projection_extent)
Lat_lon = data.frame(st_coordinates(Projection_extent)) %>%
  group_by(L2) %>%
  filter(row_number()==1)

Proj_df$lon = Lat_lon$X
Proj_df$lat = Lat_lon$Y
Proj_df$depth_m = Proj_df$Avg_Dep_m
names(Proj_df) = tolower(names(Proj_df))
#Previous runs have shown that one set of area was never sampled in the south and causes issues for predictions. removing this area from the projection data frame. 
Full_Area=ggplot()+
  geom_point(data = Proj_df[!Proj_df$centroidid %in% 
                              Proj_df[Proj_df$lat < 3664 & Proj_df$lon < 696,]$centroidid,],
       aes(x = lon, y = lat),size = .1)+
  geom_point(data = Proj_df[Proj_df$centroidid %in% 
                              Proj_df[Proj_df$lat < 3664 & Proj_df$lon < 696,]$centroidid,],
       aes(x = lon, y = lat),size = .1, colour = "red")+
  geom_sf(data= coast_outline)+
  xlim(c(min(Proj_df$lon),
         max(Proj_df$lon)))+
  ylim(c(min(Proj_df$lat),
         max(Proj_df$lat)))+
  theme_classic()+
  theme(axis.title = element_blank(),
        axis.text = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank())
Proj_df = Proj_df[!Proj_df$centroidid %in% 
                    Proj_df[Proj_df$lat < 3664 & Proj_df$lon < 696,]$centroidid,]
Rmoved_Area=ggplot()+
  geom_point(data = Proj_df,
       aes(x = lon, y = lat),size = .1)+
  geom_sf(data= coast_outline)+
  xlim(c(min(Proj_df$lon),
         max(Proj_df$lon)))+
  ylim(c(min(Proj_df$lat),
         max(Proj_df$lat)))+
    theme_classic()+
  theme(axis.title = element_blank(),
        axis.text = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank())

ggarrange(Full_Area, Rmoved_Area,ncol = 2, labels = c("A)", "B)"))

```

This projection data frame is CONSISTENT across all spatial and temporal scenarios. 

### OSW areas 

#### Spatial Scenario 1 - Small but realistic options

Here I am setting up the OSW areas for future analysis. These are the four "current" OSW WEA. 

```{r OSW current areas }
#### OSW proposed areas  - in this instance two different shapefiles for the different states, merge polygons together
# HM: edited file paths 
OSW_CA = st_read(paste0(WD.1,"/Data_shapefiles/Offshore_Wind_Energy_Lease_Outlines/Wind_Lease_Outlines.shp"), promote_to_multi=F) %>% #make sure this comes in as polygon instead of multipolygon
  st_as_sf()%>%
  filter(STATE %in% c('California',"CA")) %>%
  st_transform(crs = "+proj=utm +zone=10 +datum=WGS84 +units=km")
OSW_CA$Group = with(OSW_CA,ifelse(PROTRACTIO == "NK10-07", "Humboldt", "Morro"))#Create 2 groupings - northern and central California

# HM: edited filepath
OSW_OR = st_read(paste0(WD.1,"/Data_shapefiles/Oregon_Lease_Areas_0/Oregon_Lease_Areas_2024_08_21.shp"), promote_to_multi=F) %>% 
  st_as_sf() %>%
  st_transform(crs = "+proj=utm +zone=10 +datum=WGS84 +units=km")
OSW_OR$Group = with(OSW_OR,ifelse(Lease_ID=="B", "Brookings", "Coos Bay"))

names(OSW_CA) = tolower(names(OSW_CA))#convert to lower case 
names(OSW_OR) = tolower(names(OSW_OR))#convert to lower case 

OSW_current=dplyr::bind_rows(list(OSW_OR,OSW_CA))#Combine the two different OSW areas into one polygon object for further analysis 


```


```{r save_Spatial_Scenario_1}
saveRDS(OSW_current, paste0(WD.1, "/OSW_current.rds")) # HM note: will use this in Project 2 code
# (project 2 examines effects of closures on stock assessment and reference points)

```


#### Spatial Scenario 2 - Larger WEA areas in California

These areas are much bigger, but may not actually overlap with the surveyed region.

```{r Scenario2_save}

saveRDS(OSW_Fut, paste0(WD.1, "/OSW_Fut.rds"))
```

However, for these locations notice that how each polygon has multiple data grid cells. While this is important for the actual analysis, it makes plotting difficult. For that reason, I created polygons of just the perimeter for plotting purposes. THESE POLYGONS WILL NOT BE UTILIZED FOR MODELS BUT INSTEAD FOR PLOTTING PURPOSES  

``` {r, OutlineforMonterey}
## Starting with Monterey
unique(OSW_Fut1$PROT_NUM)
summary(st_cast(OSW_Fut %>%
          filter(group %in% "Monterey"), 'MULTILINESTRING'))
ggplot(data = OSW_Fut %>%
          filter(group %in% "Monterey") %>%
  st_buffer(dist = .1)
) +
  geom_sf(aes(colour = PROT_NUM )) 

ggplot(data = st_as_sf(as.tibble(st_coordinates(OSW_Fut %>%
  filter(group %in% "Monterey"))) %>%
  mutate(ID = paste0(round(X,5),"_", round(Y,5))) %>%
  filter(duplicated(.[["ID"]])),
  coords = c("X","Y"), crs = "+proj=utm +zone=10 +datum=WGS84 +units=km")) + 
  geom_sf(alpha = 0.1)
## Outside true 
All_Monterey = as.tibble(st_coordinates(OSW_Fut %>%
                                         filter(group %in% "Monterey"))) %>%
                mutate(ID = paste0(round(X,8),"_", round(Y,8))) %>%

df1 = All_Monterey[!All_Monterey$ID %in% Inside_Monterey$ID,c("X","Y")]

plot(st_geometry(OSW_Fut %>% filter(group %in% "Monterey")))+

Now we will look at the two additional Humboldt areas. 

```{r, OutlineforHumboldt2}

# HM: this code chunkand the next few also threw errors, and these objects are
# needed produce RDS file "OSW_Fut_outline.rds"

humboldt.2=rbind(as.data.frame(st_coordinates(OSW_Fut2 %>%
          filter(group %in% "Humboldt2"))) %>%
          mutate(X1 = as.character(round(X,8))) %>%
          group_by(X1) %>%
          summarise(Y = min(Y)) %>%
         mutate(X = as.numeric(X1))%>%
        select(X, Y) %>%
          arrange(desc(X)),
      as.data.frame(st_coordinates(OSW_Fut2 %>%
          filter(group %in% "Humboldt2"))) %>%
          mutate(X1 = as.character(round(X,8))) %>%
          group_by(X1) %>%
          summarise(Y = max(Y)) %>%
         mutate(X = as.numeric(X1)) %>%
        select(X, Y)%>%
          arrange((X)))
humboldt.2 = data.frame(rbind(humboldt.2, humboldt.2[1,]))

ggplot(data = st_cast(OSW_Fut2 %>%
          filter(group %in% "Humboldt 2"), 'MULTILINESTRING')
) +
  geom_sf() + 
  geom_point(data = as.data.frame(st_coordinates(OSW_Fut2 %>%
          filter(group %in% "Humboldt2"))) %>%
          mutate(X1 = as.character(round(X,8))) %>%
          group_by(X1) %>%
          summarise(y_min = min(Y),
                 y_max = max(Y)) %>%
         mutate(X = as.numeric(X1)), aes(x = X, y = y_min)) + 
  geom_point(data = as.data.frame(st_coordinates(OSW_Fut2 %>%
          filter(group %in% "Humboldt2"))) %>%
          mutate(X1 = as.character(round(X,8))) %>%
          group_by(X1) %>%
          summarise(y_min = min(Y),
                 y_max = max(Y)) %>%
         mutate(X = as.numeric(X1)), aes(x = X, y = y_max),
         colour = "red")+
  geom_sf(data = humboldt.2%>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("X", "Y"),
           crs = "+proj=utm +zone=10 +datum=WGS84 +units=km") %>%
  summarise(geometry = st_combine(geometry)) %>%
  st_cast("POLYGON"), fill = "transparent", colour = "blue")

Humboldt2 = humboldt.2%>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("X", "Y"),
           crs = "+proj=utm +zone=10 +datum=WGS84 +units=km") %>%
  summarise(geometry = st_combine(geometry)) %>%
  st_cast("POLYGON")
Humboldt2$group = "Humboldt2"

```

saveRDS(OSW_Large, paste0(WD.1, "/OSW_Fut_outline.rds"))

### Overlap with the projection data set

More information that would be useful if the different levels of overlap between these different proposed areas and the total area considered. This is the data included for table 1 in the manuscript. 

```{r datainformationneeded}
#Fishery data 
Catch1 = readRDS(paste0(WD.1, "/Catch_Spec_2024-11-04.rds"))
Bio1 = readRDS(paste0(WD.1, "/bio_Spec_2024-11-04.rds"))
Haul1 = readRDS(paste0(WD.1, "/haul_Spec_2024-11-04.rds"))

#Depth data 
Bathy=st_as_sf(as(raster(paste0(WD.1, "/Shapefile/Bathymetry_EPOTC.tif")), "SpatialGridDataFrame"))
Bathy = Bathy %>%
  st_transform(crs = st_crs("+proj=utm +zone=10 +datum=WGS84 +units=km"))

Projection_extent = readRDS(paste0(WD.1, "/Projection_shapefile_WCGBTWS.rds"))

```

```{r depth_area}
# Current WEAs
Bathy2 = st_intersection(OSW_current, Bathy)
Bathy2b = st_intersection(Bathy2, Projection_extent)
Bathy2b$X = st_coordinates(Bathy2b)[,1]
Bathy2b$Y = st_coordinates(Bathy2b)[,2]
Bathy2 %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(Min = as.character(min(Bathymetry_EPOTC)*-1),
            Mean = as.character(mean(Bathymetry_EPOTC)*-1),
            Max = as.character(max(Bathymetry_EPOTC)*-1))
ggplot(data = Bathy2b) + 
  geom_sf(aes(colour = Bathymetry_EPOTC))
# Proposed WEAs
Bathy3 = st_intersection(OSW_Fut, Bathy)
Bathy3b = st_intersection(Bathy3, Projection_extent)
Bathy3b$X = st_coordinates(Bathy3b)[,1]
Bathy3b$Y = st_coordinates(Bathy3b)[,2]

Bathy3 %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(Min = as.character(min(Bathymetry_EPOTC)*-1),
            Mean = as.character(mean(Bathymetry_EPOTC)*-1),
            Max = as.character(max(Bathymetry_EPOTC)*-1))


# Proposed WEAs
Bathy4 = st_intersection(OSW_Scen3, Bathy)
Bathy4b = st_intersection(Bathy4, Projection_extent)
Bathy4b$X = st_coordinates(Bathy4b)[,1]
Bathy4b$Y = st_coordinates(Bathy4b)[,2]

Bathy4 %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(Min = as.character(min(Bathymetry_EPOTC)*-1),
            Mean = as.character(mean(Bathymetry_EPOTC)*-1),
            Max = as.character(max(Bathymetry_EPOTC)*-1))

gr=st_bbox(Proj_df %>%
             st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"),
                      crs = st_crs("+proj=utm +zone=10 +datum=WGS84 +units=km"))) %>%
  st_make_grid(cellsize=.5, what='centers')%>%
  st_as_sf() %>%
  st_intersection(Projection_extent)%>%
  st_intersection(st_as_sfc(OSW_all)) 
gr_xy <- st_coordinates(gr)

for(i in 1:length(unique(OSW_all$group))){ 
  #Create a data frame for each OSW area
  gr_group[[i]]= gr %>%
    st_intersection(st_as_sfc(OSW_all[OSW_all$group==unique(OSW_all$group)[i],]))
  gr_group_xy[[i]] = st_coordinates(gr_group[[i]])
}
names(gr_group) = unique(OSW_all$group)
names(gr_group_xy) = unique(OSW_all$group)

scen_list = list()
  for(i in 1:length(gr_group_xy)){
    if(i<5){
      pred_points <- Bathy2b[Bathy2b$group %in% names(gr_group_xy)[i],] %>%
      dplyr::select(X,Y) %>% as.matrix()
      nns <- nn2(pred_points[,1:2],gr_group_xy[[i]],k=1)$nn.idx
      gr_pred <- gr_group_xy[[i]] %>% as_tibble() %>% mutate(Est=Bathy2b[Bathy2b$group %in% names(gr_group_xy)[i],]$Bathymetry_EPOTC[nns])
      gr_pred$OSW = names(gr_group_xy)[i]
      scen_list[[i]] = gr_pred
    }else if(i>=5 & i<10){
      pred_points <- Bathy3b[Bathy3b$group %in% names(gr_group_xy)[i],] %>%
        dplyr::select(X,Y) %>% as.matrix()
      nns <- nn2(pred_points[,1:2],gr_group_xy[[i]],k=1)$nn.idx
      gr_pred <- gr_group_xy[[i]] %>% as_tibble() %>% mutate(Est=Bathy3b[Bathy3b$group %in% names(gr_group_xy)[i],]$Bathymetry_EPOTC[nns])
      gr_pred$OSW = names(gr_group_xy)[i]
      scen_list[[i]] = gr_pred
    }else{
      pred_points <- Bathy4b[Bathy4b$group %in% names(gr_group_xy)[i],] %>%
        dplyr::select(X,Y) %>% as.matrix()
      nns <- nn2(pred_points[,1:2],gr_group_xy[[i]],k=1)$nn.idx
      gr_pred <- gr_group_xy[[i]] %>% as_tibble() %>% mutate(Est=Bathy4b[Bathy4b$group %in% names(gr_group_xy)[i],]$Bathymetry_EPOTC[nns])
      gr_pred$OSW = names(gr_group_xy)[i]
      scen_list[[i]] = gr_pred
    }
  }
gr_pred = bind_rows(scen_list)
```

```{r plotwithdepth}
OSW_all2 = dplyr::bind_rows(list(OSW_current, OSW_Large, OSW_Scen3))
OSW_all2 = OSW_all2 %>%
  filter(group !="Mendocino1")

oV_PLOTS = list()
for(i in 1:length(unique(OSW_all2$group))){
  oV_PLOTS[[i]]=ggplot(data = gr_pred[gr_pred$OSW %in% unique(OSW_all2$group)[i],])+
    geom_tile(aes(x = X, y = Y, fill = Est*-1))+
    xlim(min(st_coordinates(OSW_all2[OSW_all2$group==unique(OSW_all2$group)[i],])[,1]),
         max(st_coordinates(OSW_all2[OSW_all2$group==unique(OSW_all2$group)[i],])[,1]))+
    ylim(min(st_coordinates(OSW_all2[OSW_all2$group==unique(OSW_all2$group)[i],])[,2]),
         max(st_coordinates(OSW_all2[OSW_all2$group==unique(OSW_all2$group)[i],])[,2]))+
    geom_sf(data = OSW_all2[OSW_all2$group==unique(OSW_all2$group)[i],], fill = "transparent", lwd = 1, colour = "grey50")+
    #geom_sf(data = Projection_extent, fill = "transparent")+
    scale_fill_gradient2(name = "Depth (m)",
                         low = "#ffffd9", mid = "#41b6c4", high = "#081d58", midpoint = 900,
                         limits = c(max(gr_pred$Est)*-1,min(gr_pred$Est)*-1))+
    labs(title = paste0(unique(OSW_all2$group)[i]))+
    theme_classic()+
    theme(#legend.title = element_blank(),
          axis.line = element_blank(),
          axis.text = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks = element_blank(),
          axis.title = element_blank())
}

trial=grid.arrange(grid.arrange(oV_PLOTS[[2]] + 
               theme(legend.position = "none"),
             oV_PLOTS[[1]] + 
               theme(legend.position = "none"),

             oV_PLOTS[[9]] +

             oV_PLOTS[[5]] +

}
